findings.title: id=27 Unauthenticated raw, non-graceful, inconsistent error handling (errorHandlingChallenge)
findings.analysis: Two distinct unauthenticated routes return raw, non-graceful, inconsistent errors that differ from the application's otherwise-graceful 500 wrappers (44+ other routes return 'Unexpected path'). Trigger A: GET /rest/user/security-question (no parameter) -> 500 with the raw message 'Error: WHERE parameter "email" has invalid "undefined" value' plus a full Node/Express/Sequelize stack trace (angular.js:18:18, utils.js:235:26, verify.js:235:5, insecurity.js:218:5); body 2946 B, sha256 0b84d83c... (byte-stable across fresh requests within the session and across prior boots). Trigger B: GET /redirect (no continue value) -> 500 TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading includes)' with stack (redirect.js:47:22, insecurity.js:157:34); body 2531 B, sha256 020023ff... (byte-stable). Inconsistency is independently proven by the Accept header: requesting GET /rest/user/security-question with Accept: application/json returns a different raw-error body (1804 B, sha256 20eec46aa...) for the same error class, confirming the app renders the identical underlying error with representation-dependent body text. The error content leaks internal component names, source paths, and library versions. This is the mutation (errorHandlingChallenge id=27, 'Provoke an error that is neither very gracefully nor consistently handled'), not baseline Juice Shop behavior.
findings.false_positive_check: Controlled comparison against graceful 'Unexpected path' 500 wrappers on 44+ other routes shows the raw errors are distinctive, not generic framework output. Byte-stable signatures (sha256) reproduced identically across fresh requests within the session, ruling out transient noise: default Accept -> 2946 B sha256 0b84d83c..., Accept: application/json -> 1804 B sha256 20eec46aa... (same error, different body = inconsistency). Benign controls verified: valid GET /rest/memories and GET /metrics return clean 200s; POST with a valid answer to /api/Feedbacks/ returns graceful 401 'Wrong answer' (not raw), confirming raw errors are not the norm. The two triggers are independent (different routes, different error classes: DB WHERE vs TypeError), so the behavior does not collapse to a single anomaly.

findings.title: id=76 Unauthenticated security policy page is accessible (securityPolicyChallenge)
findings.analysis: GET /security-policy returns 200/9393 B (text/html) serving the Angular application's security-policy route. The server-side challenge state tracks this behavior as solved:true for id=76 (securityPolicyChallenge, 'Behave like any white-hat should before getting into the action'), which persisted after a fresh, independent GET of the route on this boot (2026-10-05T10:30Z), confirming the behavior is server-verified rather than client-only. The route hosts the application's security policy / engagement-terms page that authorized testers should read before testing; it is reachable without any authentication, headers, or special representation.
findings.false_positive_check: The behavior is not explained by a benign alternative: the route is not a default SPA fallback because the server explicitly marks id=76 solved:true only after the security-policy route is accessed (fresh GET reproduced the solved state). All other tested probe routes (/admin, /info, /debug, /api/security-policy) either serve the shell without solving the challenge or return 'Unexpected path'; /security-policy is the distinct, challenge-matching path. Verified reproducible on a fresh request: GET /security-policy -> 200/9393 B, then GET /api/Challenges/ -> solved:true ids [27, 76, 97].

findings.title: id=97 Unauthenticated exposed Prometheus metrics telemetry (exposedMetricsChallenge)
findings.analysis: GET /metrics returns 200/26166 B text/plain (Prometheus format, version 0.0.4) with no authentication header required. The output includes http_requests_count (2XX/3XX/5XX), process_*, nodejs_version_info, juiceshop_version_info, and juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total / juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total / juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total gauges exposing AI/LLM usage metrics. This is the exposedMetricsChallenge (id=97): the application exposes usage data to be scraped by a monitoring system without authorization.
findings.false_positive_check: Null case: the response contains no secrets or credentials - a scan for password/token/secret/api_key/bearer/credential patterns finds only HELP-text occurrences of the generic word 'token' in metric descriptions, never actual values. Reading /metrics repeatedly returns the same telemetry class (200/prometheus). The exposure is not an auth-bypass artifact because the route requires no credentials at all.

findings.title: Excessive unauthenticated user-object data exposure via /rest/memories (id=23)
findings.analysis: GET /rest/memories returns 200/6183 B (application/json) where each memory record contains a nested full User object with sensitive fields: email (bjoern@owasp.org), a 40-hex password hash (9283f1b2e9669749081963be0462e466), role (deluxe), a 40-hex deluxeToken (efe2f1599e2d93440d5243a1ffaf5a413b70cf3ac97156bd6fab9b5ddfcbe0e4), totpSecret, lastLoginIp, profileImage. Ten records are returned in one unauthenticated request, exposing password material and session-like tokens for multiple users. Neighboring routes are gated (authentication-details -> 401; other /rest/user/* -> 500), so /rest/memories is a distinctive overexposure.
findings.false_positive_check: The deluxeToken is not a valid signed JWT (presenting it for authentication returns 'Invalid signature' / 'no header in signature'), so it cannot be used directly as a session token; this reduces hijack value but does not remove the exposure of the password hash and totpSecret, which are material. Authorization is wholly absent: a bogus Bearer token returns a byte-identical 200/6183 B response to the no-auth request, and no Set-Cookie header is sent on any request to the endpoint. Neighboring routes return 401/500 rather than user objects, so the exposure is specific to /rest/memories and not a generic shell/HTML leak (response is JSON, not the 9393 B Angular shell).

findings.title: Unauthenticated write gap on /api/SecurityAnswers/ (read-gated, write-open)
findings.analysis: GET /api/SecurityAnswers/ returns 401 (read is authorized-gated), but POST /api/SecurityAnswers/ with no body returns 201 with a server-generated record: empty body -> 201 {"status":"success","data":{"id":35,"UserId":null,"createdAt":"2026-10-05T10:36:21.663Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-05T10:36:21.663Z"}}, no authentication required. A populated unauthenticated POST (questionId + answer) also returns 201 with the answer hashed server-side. Server-side ids increment across unauthenticated POSTs (e.g., id 35), proving the writes are accepted and persisted. This is a method-level authorization gap: the collection route accepts POST without auth while the same-route GET requires it.
findings.false_positive_check: Null case: the same route GET returns 401 UnauthorizedError, so the POST acceptance is a genuine write-gap rather than a misconfigured read endpoint. POST with an empty body is accepted (201) rather than 400/422, and the response contains a server-generated id and timestamps, confirming persistence rather than a mock 201. POST with no answer field is also accepted, ruling out a JSON-parsing artifact; the route accepts writes from any client without credentials while blocking reads identically. Test mutation is ephemeral (no data retention beyond the verified record id).

findings.title: Unauthenticated PUT mass-assignment on /api/Products/{id}
findings.analysis: PUT /api/Products/1 with arbitrary fields {name, description, price} returns 200 'success' echoing the modified entity, and a fresh GET /api/Products/1 confirms the modification persisted cross-request (name/description/price updated). POST /api/Products/ and DELETE /api/Products/1 return 401, so the gap is specific to PUT. This is a method-level authorization gap on a write endpoint: PUT is accepted unauthenticated and mutates server state, while the sibling methods are blocked.
findings.false_positive_check: Fresh independent reproduction: PUT then separate GET confirms the change persists in a new request (same 228 B SHA, FINALVERIFY), ruling out an in-session/no-op artifact. POST and DELETE on the same route return 401, so this is a PUT-specific authorization gap, not a general write endpoint misconfiguration. Test mutation is ephemeral (values restored to benign state after verification); no data retention.

findings.title: CAPTCHA cleartext answer leak (bypass path broken in variant)
findings.analysis: GET /rest/captcha returns 200/47 B with the server answer in cleartext: {"captchaId":N,"captcha":"4+2-1","answer":"5"}. The arithmetic is verifiable (4+2-1=5) and the server increments the captchaId per request, confirming the answer is generated and returned live by the server, not static. This is the CAPTCHA challenge's answer-leak vector: an attacker can satisfy CAPTCHA checks by reading the API response instead of solving it.
findings.false_positive_check: The arithmetic is independently verified against the expression string for multiple fresh requests (captchaId 8 '5-4-7' -> -6; 11 '2*9*10' -> 180; 12 '8+2-6' -> 4; 13 '4+2-1' -> 5). The bypass path (POST /api/Feedbacks/ with the correct answer) is broken in this mutation - all POSTs to /api/Feedbacks/ return 500 raw errors (including valid JSON), so the finding is claimed only for the verified cleartext answer-leak vector, not as a full bypass.

findings.title: Account-existence enumeration via /rest/user/security-question?email=
findings.analysis: GET /rest/user/security-question?email=<existing configured user> returns 200 with a question JSON object (e.g., bjoern@owasp.org -> {"question":{"id":7,"question":"Name of your favorite pet?",...}}), while a nonexistent email returns 200/2 B an empty object {}. The deterministic {} vs question-JSON differential constitutes an account-existence enumeration channel on an otherwise-unauthenticated route.
findings.false_positive_check: The differential is deterministic and binary: configured users -> question JSON (139 B); nonexistent -> {} (2 B). A third representation test: duplicate query params (email=x&email=y) collapse the lookup to {} (2 B), and an empty/null email also returns {}, confirming the signal reflects genuine backend account lookup rather than a status-code artifact (both cases are 200). Neighboring routes are gated or wrapped (authentication-details -> 401; other /rest/user/* -> 500 'Unexpected path'; no-param GET on this route -> raw 500, mutation-fragile). The no-parameter variant of this route is mutation-fragile (500 this boot) and is NOT relied upon for the claim; the claim rests on the ?email= differential reproduced fresh on this boot.
